compensating.why: hop 1 removes repeated items before passing them on
hop 2 skips parameters with an empty value
hop 4 drops a trailing unpaired item

ownership_reason: Only the gold pairs keys with values: it reads the whole sequence once, checks each key and value, and adds one parameter per key and the value after it. Hops 1, 3 and 4 hand the sequence and the list along unchanged; hop 2 adds the parameters the gold read to the request one at a time in the order given, without looking at their keys or values. Once the gold has paired 'Foo' and 'bar' with the key 'Name', the key 'Foo' can appear only if a caller discards or replaces the gold's output. The gold's javadoc promises the parameters read from a sequence of key value pairs, each key followed by its value; the variant reads ('Name', 'Val', 'Foo', 'bar') as three parameters of the key 'Name'. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling overloads HttpConnection.data(Map) and data(String, String) add one parameter per key and value; FormElement.formData adds one KeyVal per control, a repeated name giving separate parameters (FormElementTest::createsFormData: three=four, three=five); Connection.data(String...) documents .data("name", "jsoup", "language", "Java", "language", "English") as ?name=jsoup&language=Java&language=English; HttpConnectionTest::throwsOnOdddData and ::inputStream pass.
